The paper proposes a new IRS-aided electromagnetic stealth system mounted on moving targets to evade detection from multiple adversary radars.
The IRS is composed of N = N_x × N_y passive reflecting elements, each of which can be dynamically controlled to induce an independent amplitude and/or phase shift to the incident signal.
The paper formulates the problem as a convex quadratically constrained quadratic program (QCQP) that aims to minimize the sum received signal power at all adversary radars.

For the single-radar case, the paper derives a semi-closed-form optimal solution using the Lagrange multiplier method, and also proposes low-complexity closed-form solutions based on reverse alignment and minimum mean-square error (MMSE) criteria.
For the multi-radar case, the paper solves the Lagrangian dual problem to obtain a semi-closed-form optimal solution, and also proposes an MMSE-based closed-form solution.
The paper introduces an 'absorbing efficiency' parameter ζ_n to quantify the effectiveness of the n-th NIRS element in absorbing electromagnetic waves from the adversary radars.

The paper analytically determines that the minimum number of IRS elements required to achieve full electromagnetic stealth is N = ⌈|C|/β_max⌉ + 1, where C is the complex-valued reflection gain at the NIRS and β_max is the maximum reflection amplitude of each IRS element.

The simulation results show that the proposed IRS-aided electromagnetic stealth system significantly reduces and even eliminates the signal reflected by the target, achieving satisfactory stealth performance.

The paper investigates the impact of imperfect angle-of-arrival information at the target and shows that the proposed system can still outperform traditional approaches in reducing the received signal power at the radars.

The key advantages of the proposed IRS-aided electromagnetic stealth system are its flexibility, adaptability, wide operating range, and cost-effectiveness compared to traditional fixed electromagnetic stealth materials.
The paper proposes practical low-complexity estimation schemes at the target to acquire the necessary angle-of-arrival and/or path gain information for the IRS's reflection design.
The proposed IRS-aided electromagnetic stealth system is shown to be effective in evading detection from multiple distributed radars in highly dynamic military scenarios.
The paper demonstrates the potential of IRS technology in complementing or assisting imperfect electromagnetic stealth in time-varying and complex wireless environments.
The proposed IRS-aided electromagnetic stealth system can be readily extended to the case of multiple moving targets, each equipped with an independent IRS-aided stealth system.

The paper provides a comprehensive analysis and design of the IRS-aided electromagnetic stealth system, covering problem formulation, optimization algorithms, practical estimation schemes, and performance evaluation.
